threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of Stoke Newington. The locals will let you know there's a difference.
Heard a lad on the 3 bus saying he lost his phone trying to impress someone at the Prince Albert—never saw him get off. Brixton nights are wild.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was a local? When a street artist asked me for tips on the best coffee spots—not the other way around.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find graffiti art and flower markets happening side by side on a Tuesday morning, where every corner tells a different story.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate the bus delays—grabbing a taco and rolling their eyes at yet another 14-Mission late arrival.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling flaming torches on the 9 bus while debating the best burrito in the city—only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Sagrada Família is the heart of Barcelona, but Gràcia’s plazas hold the real vibe. It's where the locals unwind and share secrets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their reluctance to try a 'bocata' standing up at the bar. True locals know it's part of the experience.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's weird when a shop closes at 5 PM, while the pub stays open till midnight. Welcome to Dalston, mate!
Last night on the 59, a bloke in a panda onesie serenaded the driver with a guitar. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the local kids setting up a street festival with makeshift stalls and thrifted decorations—there's creativity in chaos that only feels like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 2 AM, then debate art with a street musician while the U-Bahn is on strike. It's a vibe like no other.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they happily dodge the BART delays but still know the best taco spot within a two-block radius.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full clown makeup on the 6 bus, juggling oranges while explaining his philosophy on happiness. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all hip bars and trendy shops. They miss the quiet corners where old ladies gossip over café amb llet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they struggle to find the right 'tapa' at the bar, still asking for 'tapas' like it’s a buffet.
